entry.title: Tech, labor, and token costs: the new AI math

media:group.media:title: Tech, labor, and token costs: the new AI math
media:group.media:description:
In this WorkLab podcast clip, Andy Doyle, Kantar's Chief People and Agent Officer, lays out the new math facing enterprises: tech cost, labor cost, and token cost—and how to triangulate all three in a way that makes sense.
The real question isn't the individual budgets, it's what this costs you overall—and where you deploy technology and super agents versus where you put people. Until now, that choice was forced on you by the availability of technology and the skillsets you had. Now leaders have real choices to make about how to deploy people in the best way.

entry.title: The AI skill everyone should have

media:group.media:title: The AI skill everyone should have
media:group.media:description:
In this WorkLab podcast clip, Andy Doyle, Kantar's Chief People and Agent Officer, explains why deploying AI isn't the same as adopting it. Most tech organizations can say they've turned it on and put Copilot in the ecosystem—but that's not where adoption happens.
The real gap is skills and fear: people don't know how to experiment, and they're scared to fail or to build an agent. Doyle's takeaway from building agents himself—you're not failing, you're iterating. You just haven't succeeded yet.

entry.title: This company has more AI agents than employees

media:group.media:title: This company has more AI agents than employees
media:group.media:description:
When market research firm Kantar handed Copilot licenses to every employee, chaos and creativity erupted. Andy Doyle, Kantar Chief People and Agent Officer, joins the WorkLab podcast to share how a wave of maverick experimentation led to 15,000 agents—and the birth of an "agent factory" that's reshaping the enterprise.
Hear how frontline innovators, influencer evangelists, and a wild diversity of agent builders forced leaders to rethink control, scalability, and what's possible when you let people drive the AI transformation.

entry.title: What CEOs are quietly admitting about AI

media:group.media:title: What CEOs are quietly admitting about AI
media:group.media:description:
In this WorkLab podcast clip, Allie K. Miller, AI leader, investor, and former Global Head of Machine Learning at AWS, calls out a growing leadership gap: many executives are setting AI strategy and driving AI transformation without hands-on experience using AI tools and agents themselves.
The result? Missed opportunities and strategies that don't translate into real change. The strongest organizations combine top-down vision with bottom-up experimentation to accelerate AI adoption, build effective AI strategies, and unlock business transformation.

media:group.media:title: The biggest AI mistake?
media:group.media:description:
In this WorkLab podcast clip, Allie K. Miller, AI leader, investor, and former Global Head of Machine Learning at AWS, explains why treating AI like traditional software limits its impact.
Real transformation happens when organizations rethink business models, processes, and entire operating structures—not just productivity gains.

entry.title: 3 skills you need in the age of AI

media:group.media:title: 3 skills you need in the age of AI
media:group.media:description:
In this WorkLab podcast clip, Allie K. Miller, CEO of Open Machine and former Global Head of Machine Learning at AWS, shares the three skillsets she looks for in an AI-first world: high agency, a strong sense of curiosity, and systems thinking.
It’s not just about using AI tools. It’s about how you experiment, adapt, and navigate increasingly complex, multi-agent systems. As AI adoption accelerates, these skills are becoming essential for professionals and leaders to succeed in an AI-powered workplace.

media:group.media:title: The sound of survival
media:group.media:description:
There are only 75 southern resident orcas left in the world, and they rely on sound to survive.
Bioacoustics is helping protect their habitat in Washington's Salish Sea by helping to reduce underwater noise. Microsoft recently partnered with Sea Mammal Research Unit Consulting and Washington Maritime Blue to search for the acoustic signatures of marine life beneath the waves—sending AI-powered, real-time alerts to mariners to slow down their ships to reduce underwater noise pollution.
What once took weeks or days to analyze, AI can now process in minutes. For critically endangered species, those minutes can make all the difference.
Get the full story on Unlocked and discover how AI is helping protect endangered orcas through real-time acoustic monitoring and conservation technology.
Learn More at Unlocked - https://unlocked.microsoft.com/blue-sparrow-orca-conservation/
